name: Cox's Bazar
tagline: The longest beach in the land — golden sand running unbroken for miles, the coral of Saint Martin's, the Buddhist temples of Ramu, and the Marine Drive threading between the hills and the Bay of Bengal.

guide.bestTime: November to March — dry, cool and clear, with calm seas. Saint Martin's is only reachable in this window, and even then under tight government limits; Adinath's big fair at Maheshkhali falls in Phalgun (Feb–Mar).
guide.gettingThere: Cox's Bazar is one of the few districts reachable every way: by road from Dhaka (~400 km) and Chattogram, by the new railway to the oyster-shaped Iconic Station (the Dohazari–Cox's Bazar line opened in 2023), and by domestic flights to Cox's Bazar Airport. Ships to Saint Martin's run seasonally from Teknaf.
guide.difficulty: Easy in and around town and along Marine Drive; moderate for Saint Martin's and the islands, which depend on seasonal, weather-dependent and currently restricted boat travel.

mustVisit.name: Cox's Bazar Sea Beach
mustVisit.description: The headline of the whole district — a band of golden sand often called the world's longest natural unbroken sea beach, running roughly 120 km down the coast, with the surf of the Bay of Bengal rolling in.
mustVisit.history: The beach made Cox's Bazar the country's premier seaside resort. Its named stretches — Laboni nearest the town, then Sugandha and Kolatoli — gather the crowds, the deck chairs and the sunset-watchers, while the sand runs on far quieter to the south.

practical.hours: Open all day; lifeguard flags mark safe bathing zones

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: Laboni Point is the town beach; Sugandha and Kolatoli are a short ride south
howToReach.transport: Walk, rickshaw or auto within town

mustVisit.bestTime: Sunset; cool, dry months for calm seas
tips: Swim only between the lifeguard flags — currents can be strong
Laboni is busiest; head south for quieter sand
Sunset is the moment everyone gathers for

mustVisit.name: Himchari National Park & Waterfall
mustVisit.description: Where the hills meet the sea just south of town — a forested national park with a seasonal waterfall and viewpoints looking out over the Bay of Bengal.
mustVisit.history: Himchari protects a stretch of coastal hill forest along Marine Drive. Its waterfall is fullest in and just after the rains, and the ridge-top viewpoints give some of the best sea panoramas near Cox's Bazar.

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: ~12 km south of town on Marine Drive
howToReach.transport: Auto, CNG or car along Marine Drive

mustVisit.bestTime: Just after the monsoon for the waterfall; clear days for the views
tips: The waterfall shrinks in the dry season — temper expectations in winter
Combine it with a Marine Drive run toward Inani

mustVisit.name: Inani Beach
mustVisit.description: A long, golden beach down the coast famed for its smooth sand and the boulder and coral-rock formations exposed at low tide — quieter and wilder than the town beaches.
mustVisit.history: Inani, with the rocky stretch at Patuartek just to its north, lies along Marine Drive in Ukhia and has become the favourite escape from the busier town sand, especially at low tide when the rocks emerge.

practical.hours: Daytime; check tide times for the rocks

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: ~35 km south of town on Marine Drive (Ukhia)
howToReach.transport: Car, CNG or auto along Marine Drive

mustVisit.bestTime: Low tide for the boulders; cool months
tips: Time your visit for low tide to see the rock and coral formations
The drive itself, between hills and sea, is half the pleasure

mustVisit.name: Marine Drive
mustVisit.description: The ~80 km coastal road from Cox's Bazar to Teknaf — the Bay of Bengal on one side, green hills on the other — one of the most scenic drives in the country.
mustVisit.history: Built along the shoreline, Marine Drive strings together the district's beaches and viewpoints — Himchari, Inani, Patuartek, Shamlapur — all the way to the southern tip at Teknaf on the Naf River.

practical.hours: Daylight for the views; drive carefully after dark

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: Starts at the south edge of Cox's Bazar town
howToReach.transport: Hire a car, CNG or open jeep

mustVisit.bestTime: Morning or late afternoon for the light on the sea
tips: An open jeep makes the most of the views
Stop at Himchari, Inani and the small fishing beaches along the way

mustVisit.name: Saint Martin's Island (Narikel Jinjira)
mustVisit.description: Bangladesh's only coral island — a small, palm-fringed isle of turquoise water, reefs and beaches off the southern tip, reached by ship from Teknaf.
mustVisit.history: Saint Martin's (Narikel Jinjira, 'coconut island') sits where the Naf River meets the Bay. Its corals have suffered heavy degradation, so the government now tightly restricts tourism — limiting numbers, day-trips and overnight stays by season, and closing the island entirely during part of the year.

practical.hours: Seasonal access only (roughly Nov–Mar) under government caps; verify before travel

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: Off the southern tip; ship from Teknaf (~2.5 hr), itself ~80 km from town
howToReach.transport: Bus/car to Teknaf, then a seasonal tourist ship

mustVisit.bestTime: The narrow winter window the island is open — confirm the current rules first
tips: Critical: check the current access rules before you plan — overnight stays and tourist numbers are capped, and the island closes for part of the year
Don't touch or take coral or shells — the reef is protected and fragile
Book ship tickets and any permitted stay well ahead

mustVisit.name: Maheshkhali Island
mustVisit.description: The country's only notably hilly island, across the channel from town — home to the hilltop Adinath Shiva temple, Rakhine Buddhist pagodas, salt pans and the famously sweet betel leaf.
mustVisit.history: On Mainak hill stands the Adinath Temple, whose Phalgun-month fair draws great crowds of Hindu pilgrims; nearby Buddhist monasteries reflect the island's Rakhine community. Maheshkhali is renowned across the country for its mishti paan (sweet betel leaf).

practical.hours: Daytime; the Adinath fair is in Phalgun (Feb–Mar)

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: Across the channel; speedboat or engine-boat from the Cox's Bazar jetty

mustVisit.bestTime: Phalgun for the Adinath fair; cool months otherwise
tips: Buy the famous Maheshkhali paan to take home
Combine the temple, the pagodas and the salt fields in one trip

mustVisit.name: Ramu Buddhist Village
mustVisit.description: A centre of living Buddhist heritage near town — dozens of temples and monasteries, a great golden reclining Buddha and an old bronze image, set among the homes of the Barua Buddhist community.
mustVisit.history: Ramu has long been a heart of Buddhist culture in the region, with monasteries such as Ramkot (Rangkut) Banashram among the oldest in the country. Temples damaged in communal attacks in 2012 were subsequently rebuilt, and the village remains a place of worship, craft and festival.

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: ~25 km east of Cox's Bazar town, Ramu upazila
howToReach.transport: Bus, CNG or car from town

mustVisit.bestTime: Buddhist full-moon festivals; mornings for quiet
tips: Dress modestly and remove shoes in the temples
Be respectful — these are active places of worship

mustVisit.name: Dulahazara Safari Park
mustVisit.description: Bangladesh's first safari park, at Dulahazara in Chakaria — where animals roam in large open enclosures and visitors drive or walk through the forest setting.
mustVisit.history: Opened as a safari park in the early 2000s on the site of an earlier deer-breeding centre, Dulahazara holds tigers, lions, elephants, deer and many birds across its forested grounds in the north of the district.

practical.hours: Daytime; closed on its weekly off-day

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: Dulahazara, Chakaria upazila, ~50 km north of town

mustVisit.bestTime: Cool, dry months; mornings for active animals
tips: Go early when the animals are most active
Good for families; allow a few hours for the grounds

specialties.name: Shutki (Dried Fish)
specialties.description: Cox's Bazar's most authentic flavour — sea fish sun-dried on the vast racks of Nazirartek, the largest dried-fish yard in the region, and cooked into pungent, fiery shutki bhuna and bhorta.
specialties.venue: Nazirartek dried-fish market and local kitchens

specialties.name: Maheshkhali Mishti Paan
specialties.description: The sweet betel leaf of Maheshkhali island, renowned across the country and sold all along the beach front.
specialties.venue: Maheshkhali island and Cox's Bazar town

specialties.name: Adinath Mela
specialties.description: The great fair at the hilltop Adinath Shiva temple on Maheshkhali, drawing crowds of pilgrims and traders in the month of Phalgun.

bucketlist.title: Drive the full Marine Drive to Teknaf
bucketlist.detail: ~80 km of coast road with the sea on one side and hills on the other — best in an open jeep.

bucketlist.title: Reach the coral island of Saint Martin's
bucketlist.detail: Bangladesh's only coral island — turquoise water and reefs off the southern tip. Access is seasonal and government-capped, so check the current rules first.

bucketlist.title: See the rocks at Inani at low tide
bucketlist.detail: Golden sand and exposed boulder-and-coral formations down the coast at Inani and Patuartek.

bucketlist.title: Climb to a viewpoint at Himchari
bucketlist.detail: Coastal hill forest, a seasonal waterfall and big sea views just south of town.

bucketlist.title: Boat to Maheshkhali island
bucketlist.detail: The hilltop Adinath Shiva temple, Rakhine Buddhist pagodas, salt pans and the famous sweet paan.

bucketlist.title: See the Buddhist temples of Ramu

bucketlist.detail: Grilled squid, prawns and rupchanda straight off the boats at the Kolatoli food stalls.

foods.name: Shutki Bhuna & Bhorta
foods.description: Sun-dried sea fish cooked into pungent, fiery curries and mashes — the most authentic Cox's Bazar flavour.

foods.name: Fresh Grilled Seafood
foods.description: Squid, prawns, rupchanda and sea fish grilled fresh at the beach-front stalls.

foods.name: Maheshkhali Mishti Paan

foods.name: Rakhine Cuisine
foods.description: The local Rakhine community's cooking — sticky rice, spicy fish soups and dishes built on nappi (fermented shrimp paste).
foods.whereToFind: Rakhine para eateries in and around town

famousPeople.name: Captain Hiram Cox
famousPeople.knownFor: The district's namesake — an East India Company officer sent in 1799 to resettle Arakanese refugees fleeing Burmese persecution. He died before completing the work, and a market raised in his memory ('Cox's Bazar', Cox's market) gave the place its name.

famousPeople.name: Masudul Hoq
famousPeople.knownFor: Contemporary Bengali poet, short-story writer and translator associated with Cox's Bazar.

didYouKnow: Cox's Bazar has the beach often called the world's longest natural unbroken sea beach, commonly cited at around 120 km.
The district is named after Captain Hiram Cox, an East India Company officer who in 1799 set about resettling Arakanese refugees on this coast.
Saint Martin's Island is Bangladesh's only coral island — and is now under strict seasonal tourism limits to protect its damaged reefs.
Maheshkhali is the country's only notably hilly island, famous for its sweet betel leaf (paan) and the hilltop Adinath Shiva temple.
Cox's Bazar got its first-ever railway in 2023 — the oyster-shaped Iconic Railway Station, the terminus of the new Dohazari–Cox's Bazar line.
